title: Measure and reduce context amplification in long-running agent workflows
observation: Long agent runs repeatedly process prior context, tool output, worker reports, and shared parent context. This can create superlinear cumulative token usage and multiplicative duplication across fan-out, retries, and review loops. Existing EVR-0013 / DEC-0018 evidence already measured roughly 68% lower tokens and latency from focused delegate attachments at equal accuracy.
suspected_root_cause: Context is often optimized per call rather than across the complete run, so repeated history, tool output, fan-out duplication, retries, and review loops can amplify total input far beyond unique useful information.
suggested_direction: Instrument context amplification first, benchmark raw-history vs compiled/retrieved/checkpointed context, then promote only provenance-preserving reductions that lower total tokens/cost/latency without degrading validated outcomes.
acceptance: Orchestrator reports cumulative input tokens and context amplification for representative runs
Synthetic long-session and multi-agent fan-out benchmarks demonstrate current scaling behavior
At least one context strategy is compared against the incumbent with identical validators
Winning optimizations are promoted only when validation is noninferior and total cost per successful task improves
Context provenance and checkpoint/resume correctness are preserved
Context-window size is treated as a measured resource rather than a target to fill
risks: Over-compaction can remove information needed for correctness or debugging
Token reductions can be offset by retries or stronger-model escalations
Provider cache accounting may be unavailable or provider-specific

source.reference: 2026-09-29 explicit request to prioritize context-window/token amplification testing

notes: High priority, measurement first, no paid compute required for initial benchmarks.
